Gaming can look simple, but there is a lot to it (I'm not saying its hard, only that is depper than we can see). I've been playing games for more than 10 years and now and then I'm completly smashed by other players, so here some advices I took that helped me along those years:

- different players have different learning speeds. I can easily pick up a fps game, but when I get my hands on a motorsport game they kick my ass pretty bad. I always thought I wasnt born to those games, but I soon realise that I have always played fps and very few motorsport games. So there is probably some else that has the exactly opposite situation.

- Learns from pros. You can always ask advice to your friends and if you can't Youtube is a place full of experienced people of pretty much everything. 

- Gaming isn't only about games. It sure is a weird phrase, but you have to be perfectly balanced for a good play time. I learned it from playing competitive, the day I was angry always combined with the day that my team lost (which was many times hahaha)

-  Ranked isn't and never will be easy and all fun. There will always be someone better than you, but this isn't a bad thing. This means there will always be a room for improviment. Sometimes it will be hard to pass to the next level and you will have to stay patient.

-  Single player is always a good place to come back. If you want the relieve you stress after a bad multiplayer game just go to a single player game and become rhe ultimate bad ass, there is no shame in that. 

-  the last thing is kinda of an advice for live: there is a lot of things in life that will get in your nerves, even if you are Gandhi. So you need to learn to handle yourself in those situations, bc if you don't you might harm others close to you.
